cards.explanation: The answer is her husband and children. God says Jerusalem is the daughter of her mother, who "…despised her husband and children." (Ezekiel 16:45) That's the family resemblance the proverb points to. I think this one is heavy, because it's about turning away from the people closest to you.

The answer is Samaria. God says, "Your older sister was Samaria, who lived with her daughters to your north…" (Ezekiel 16:46) Samaria is the older sister here, and she had her daughters with her. Jerusalem's family is bigger than just the one sister, friends.

The answer is Sodom. God says, "…your younger sister was Sodom, who lived with her daughters to your south." (Ezekiel 16:46) So Jerusalem has an older sister to the north and a younger one to the south. She's sitting right in the middle of the family photo.

The answer is that she became more depraved than they were. God says she walked in their ways and practiced their abominations, "…but soon you were more depraved than they were." (Ezekiel 16:47) She didn't just follow her sisters, friends. She went further than they did. I think this verse is a heavy one.

The answer is True. God says Sodom and her daughters "…did not help the poor and needy." (Ezekiel 16:49) They were arrogant, overfed and complacent, and that's the iniquity God names. Notice that He lists it plainly, with no extra commentary needed.

The answer is righteous. God says her abominations "…have made your sisters appear righteous." (Ezekiel 16:51) That's how far Jerusalem went, friends. She made Samaria and Sodom look better just by standing next to them.

The answer is False. God says, "So you too must bear your shame and disgrace, since you have made your sisters appear righteous." (Ezekiel 16:52) Her sisters looking better doesn't lift anything off her. Jerusalem has to carry it herself.

The answer is False. God says He will restore Sodom and Samaria, and then adds, "And I will restore you along with them." (Ezekiel 16:53) Jerusalem is right there with her sisters. After all that heavy talk, friends, that's quite the turn.

The answer is ashamed. God says, "So you will bear your disgrace and be ashamed of all you did to comfort them." (Ezekiel 16:54) The word is ashamed, and it comes right after the promise to restore. I think that shows she'll see her past plainly.

The answer is as an object of scorn. God asks, "Did you not treat your sister Sodom as an object of scorn in the day of your pride…" (Ezekiel 16:56) That was before her own wickedness was uncovered. I think this one stings a little, friends.

The answer is the oath, by breaking the covenant. God says, "I will deal with you according to your deeds, since you have despised the oath by breaking the covenant." (Ezekiel 16:59) The oath and the covenant go together here. She broke what she had sworn to keep.

The answer is True, and what a turn that is. God says, "…I will remember the covenant I made with you in the days of your youth…" (Ezekiel 16:60) She broke the covenant, and He still says He will remember it. That one gets me every time, friends.

The answer is everlasting. God says, "…I will establish an everlasting covenant with you." (Ezekiel 16:60) Everlasting means it doesn't run out. After a broken covenant, friends, that's a big promise to hear.

The answer is True. God says, "I will give them to you as daughters, but not because of My covenant with you." (Ezekiel 16:61) That's in the same verse where Jerusalem remembers her ways and is ashamed when she receives her older and younger sisters. The family gets bigger, friends.

The answer is that He is the LORD. God says, "So I will establish My covenant with you, and you will know that I am the LORD…" (Ezekiel 16:62) The knowing is about who He is. It's a good place for this long message to land, friends.

The answer is True. God says that when He makes atonement for all she has done, she will "…never again open your mouth because of your disgrace…" (Ezekiel 16:63) That's the last line of the message, friends. The one who makes atonement is God Himself.
